Title: Engaging Mathematics Educatorsa
NewsSummary: The Institute of Educational Development in East Africa has been nominated as the host and leading partner for the International Commission on Mathematical Instruction's fourth Capacity and Network Planning Conference.

content.text: The Institute of Educational Development in East Africa has been nominated as the host and leading partner for the International Commission on Mathematical Instruction's fourth Capacity and Network Planning Conference (CANP4). The two-week conference will be held from September 1-12, 2014 in Dar es Salaam, at the IED campus, and will be attended by mathematics educators from Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda.
In preparation for CANP4, a meeting of the Local Organising Committee chaired by Professor Anjum Halai, Head of Research at IED, was held from February 24-26.

ICMI President, Professor Ferdinando Arzarello, from Tourino University, Italy, attended the session as did mathematics education experts from across the region. These included Dr Alphonse Uworwabayeho from the Kigali Institute of Education, Rwanda; Masaba Nasur Mwambu from SESEMAT (Science and Mathematics Teachers' Programme), Uganda; Patrick Kogola from the Centre for Mathematics, Science and Technology Education in Africa, Kenya; Dr Sylvester E. Rugeihyamu, President of the Mathematics Association of Tanzania; and Silas Mirau from the Nelson Mandela African Institute of Science and Technology in Tanzania.

IED, EA was represented by its SIGMAS (Special Interest Group in Mathematics and Science Education) team members: Dr Geoff Tennant, Peter Kajoro, Veronica Sarungi, Dr Simon Karuku and Mussa Muhamed. SIGMAS is a vibrant group of researchers and academicians keenly interested in improving the quality of mathematics and science education in East Africa.

CANP4 will soon be recruiting 50 leading mathematics teachers and teacher educators from across the four countries for this exciting event. The programme will include invited guest lectures demonstrating mathematical modelling on real life issues related to mathematics for Planet Earth, in addition to presentations from SIGMAS members reflecting on work on mathematics education in the region.
A series of teacher development workshops will be organised to engage participants in mathematical activities who will also get the opportunity to devise their own activities.
One of the goals of the conference is to set-up a regional network with a series of follow up events, in order to sustain and develop the work undertaken at CANP4.
